From 243b467dea1735fed904c2e54d248a46fa417a2d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bert Karwatzki <spasswolf@web.de>
Date: Sun, 1 Feb 2026 01:24:45 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] Revert "drm/amd: Check if ASPM is enabled from PCIe
 subsystem"
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

This reverts commit 7294863a6f01248d72b61d38478978d638641bee.

This commit was erroneously applied again after commit 0ab5d711ec74
("drm/amd: Refactor `amdgpu_aspm` to be evaluated per device")
removed it, leading to very hard to debug crashes, when used with a system with two
AMD GPUs of which only one supports ASPM.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-acpi/20251006120944.7880-1-spasswolf@web.de/
Link: https://github.com/acpica/acpica/issues/1060
Fixes: 0ab5d711ec74 ("drm/amd: Refactor `amdgpu_aspm` to be evaluated per device")
Signed-off-by: Bert Karwatzki <spasswolf@web.de>
Reviewed-by: Christian König <christian.koenig@amd.com>
Reviewed-by: Mario Limonciello (AMD) <superm1@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Mario Limonciello <mario.limonciello@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>
(cherry picked from commit 97a9689300eb2b393ba5efc17c8e5db835917080)
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_drv.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_drv.c
index 6ccb80e2d7c9..39387da8586b 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_drv.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_drv.c
@@ -2405,9 +2405,6 @@ static int amdgpu_pci_probe(struct pci_dev *pdev,
 			return -ENODEV;
 	}
 
-	if (amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev))
-		amdgpu_aspm = 0;
-
 	if (amdgpu_virtual_display ||
 	    amdgpu_device_asic_has_dc_support(pdev, flags & AMD_ASIC_MASK))
 		supports_atomic = true;
-- 
2.34.1

This patch reverts commit 7294863a6f01 ("drm/amd: Check if ASPM is enabled from PCIe subsystem"), which was erroneously reapplied after a prior refactoring had removed it. The reversion addresses hard-to-debug crashes occurring on systems with two AMD GPUs where only one supports ASPM.

**Modification in `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_drv.c`**:
- Removed the following two lines from the `amdgpu_pci_probe` function:
  ```c
  if (amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev))
      amdgpu_aspm = 0;
  ```
  This conditional previously set `amdgpu_aspm` to 0 (disabling ASPM) when the module parameter was at its default (-1) and the PCIe subsystem reported that ASPM was not enabled for the device.

**Relationship**:
The removal eliminates the automatic per-device ASPM disablement logic that had been introduced in the reverted commit. This logic caused system instability (crashes) in multi-GPU configurations because it incorrectly applied a global override based on one device’s ASPM status, ignoring that other GPUs might still depend on ASPM. The patch restores the previous behavior where ASPM handling is solely controlled by the module parameter and existing per-device checks elsewhere.

Root cause:
The reverted commit introduced a global override of the `amdgpu_aspm` module parameter based on a single device's ASPM status (`!pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)`). On systems with multiple AMD GPUs where only one supports ASPM, this incorrectly disables ASPM for all GPUs, leading to crashes due to inconsistent ASPM configurations.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
if (amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev))
    amdgpu_aspm = 0;
Reason: These lines globally modify the `amdgpu_aspm` module parameter based on a single device's ASPM capability. On systems with multiple AMD GPUs where only one supports ASPM, this incorrectly disables ASPM for all devices, leading to inconsistent ASPM states and crashes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
-       if (amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev))
-               amdgpu_aspm = 0;
Reason: Removing these two lines reverts the erroneous global override. This restores per-device ASPM evaluation, so each GPU's ASPM setting is determined independently based on its own capabilities, eliminating the crash on multi-GPU systems.
